question: A shopkeeper bought two pairs of shoes at the same price and sold one pair at a profit of 15% and the other pair at a loss of 5%. if the difference between their selling prices is ₹140, then how much profit did he earn in the whole transaction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the cost price (CP) of each pair of shoes be 100%.

The selling prices are 115% (15% profit) and 95% (5% loss).

Difference in selling price = 115% − 95% = 20%.

Given 20% = ₹140 ⇒ 10% = ₹70.

Overall net profit = (+15%) − 5% = +10%.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93a2652b6d2f3295c124fa989385421e29efa06563b98ffa689528a1b3c0b3a7.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ The cost price of both pairs of shoes is exactly the same.

⇒ Profit earned on the first pair = 15%

⇒ Loss incurred on the second pair = 5%

⇒ Difference between their selling prices = ₹140

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price (CP) of each pair be 100 units.

⇒ Selling price of the first pair (SP₁) = 100 + 15% of 100 = 115 units

⇒ Selling price of the second pair (SP₂) = 100 − 5% of 100 = 95 units

⇒ Difference in selling prices = 115 units − 95 units = 20 units

⇒ Since 20 units corresponds to ₹140:

⇒ 1 unit = 140 ÷ 20 = ₹7

⇒ Cost Price of each pair = 100 × 7 = ₹700

⇒ Total profit earned = Profit on first pair − Loss on second pair

⇒ Total net profit = 15 units − 5 units = 10 units

⇒ Overall net profit = 10 × 7 = ₹70

**∴ The correct answer is ₹70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same Cost Price Rule

When two items are bought at the same Cost Price, the overall profit or loss percentage is the simple average of their individual profit and loss percentages.

Same Selling Price Rule

When two items are sold at the exact same Selling Price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall net loss given by the formula (x² ÷ 100)%.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit and Loss are always inherently calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the problem. Profit = SP − CP, and Loss = CP − SP.
